mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
regime_hint: FED Funds rate above 4% target zone
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a 0% baseline (p > 0.05) during FEDFUNDS > 4% periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as stronger hiring signals robust economic growth and investor optimism.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS vs. SPX 60-day returns < 0.05 over 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in HOUST (industrial production) by at least 2% in the prior month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing demand raises recession risk.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite HOUST decline (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 1% for two consecutive months increases the 60-day S&P 500 forward return by anticipating supply-side expansion and demand recovery.
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO trend and SPX 60-day returns (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in RSAFS (money supply) of 2% or more over the last 3 months trigger a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return via expectations of tighter liquidity.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < previous month's value by ≥ 2% for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: Accelerating contraction in broad money supply
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive during such contraction periods (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.5% in the prior month, accompanied by rising GDPC1 (personal consumption), predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 return as labor market tightening supports growth expectations.
regime_hint: Labor market tightening with robust consumption
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return when both triggers are met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month for the second consecutive month, the 60-day S&P 500 forward return is expected to be negative due to inflation concerns and risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous month by > 0.5% and same for prior month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive despite the CPI trigger (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a 'late-cycle expansion' as indicated by a 3-month moving average of GDPC1 above 1.5% growth and PAYEMS > 130,000, predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return from optimism about sustained demand and production.
failure_condition: No positive 20-day returns in late-cycle expansion regime (p > 0.05).
